{{Short description|German-Jewish mathematician}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=September 2022}}
[[File:Emil Hilb 1908.gif|thumb|Emil Hilb 1908]]

'''Emil Hilb''' (born 26 April 1882 in Stuttgart;<ref>{{citation|contribution=Lebenslauf|first=E.|last=Hilb|title=Beiträge zur theorie der lame'schen Funktionen|year=1903|page=60|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ls4TAQAAIAAJ&pg=PA60}}.</ref> died 6 August 1929<ref>{{citation|title=Notes|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|volume=35|year=1929|issue=6|pages=885–888|doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1929-04829-8|doi-access=free}}.</ref> in Würzburg) was a German-Jewish<ref>{{citation|title=Juden in Würzburg, 1918–1933|volume=34|series=Mainfränkische Studien|first=Roland|last=Flade|edition=2nd|year=1985|page=47}}.</ref> mathematician who worked in the fields of [[special function]]s, [[differential equation]]s, and [[difference equation]]s.  He was one of the authors of the ''Enzyklopädie der mathematischen Wissenschaften'' (''Encyclopedia of mathematical sciences''), contributing on the topics of [[trigonometric series]] and differential equations.  He wrote a book on [[Lamé function]]s.<ref name="HJV">http://www.didaktik.mathematik.uni-wuerzburg.de/history/vollrath/papers/073.pdf Hans-Joachim Vollrath: Emil Hilb (1882–1929), In: P. Baumgart (Hrsg.), Lebensbilder bedeutender Würzburger Professoren, Neustadt/Aisch (Degener), 1995, pages 320–338</ref>

Hilb obtained his PhD in 1903 under the supervision of [[Ferdinand von Lindemann]].<ref name="mg">{{mathgenealogy|id=19493}}</ref> He worked as a high school mathematics teacher in [[Augsburg]] until 1906, when [[Max Noether]] hired him as an assistant; in 1908 he found a position as a lecturer at the [[University of Erlangen]]. He won a position as a professor at the [[University of Würzburg]] in 1909, in preference over [[Ernst Zermelo]].<ref>{{citation|title=Collected Works: Volume I|first=Ernst|last=Zermelo|publisher=Springer-Verlag|year=2009|isbn=978-3-540-79383-0|page=19|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XB2nd2ovakIC&pg=PA19}}.</ref> His students at Würzburg included [[Richard J. Bär|Richard Bär]], who later became a distinguished experimental physicist,<ref>{{citation|title=Erwin Schrödinger and the Rise of Wave Mechanics: Schrödinger in Vienna and Zurich 1887–1925, Part 1|series=The historical development of quantum theory|first1=Jagdish|last1=Mehra|first2=Helmut|last2=Rechenberg|author-link1=Jagdish Mehra |author-link2=Helmut Rechenberg |publisher=Springer-Verlag|year=2001|isbn=978-0-387-95179-9|page=285|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=AwmQTGB8LwMC&pg=PA285}}.</ref> [[Otto Haupt]], and Axel Schur.<ref name="HJV"/><ref name="mg"/>

== Books ==

* ''Beiträge zur theorie der [[Lamé function|lame'schen Funktionen]]'' (Contributions to the theory of [[Lamé function]]s), München, 1903
* ''Über Integraldarstellungen willkürlicher Funktionen'' (On integral representations of arbitrary functions), Teubner, 1908
* [https://web.archive.org/web/20160201215205/http://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/no_cache/dms/load/toc/?IDDOC=193092 ''Enzyklopädie der mathematischen Wissenschaften'' (Encyclopedia of the Mathematical Sciences), second volume, edited by H. Burkhardt, W. Wirtinger, R. Fricke, and E. Hilb – downloadable pdf files from the University of Göttingen] (German)
